en.name: Cooking wine
en.summary: Bottled cooking wine — Taiwanese rice wine, Shaoxing, salted cooking wines and grape-based cooking wines — has no fixed shelf life. At 10 percent alcohol or more it is not a food that spoils dangerously; keep it capped in a cool, dark cupboard. What you lose after opening is aroma, not safety.
en.pantry: The cupboard is the right place and the honest answer is a rule, not a number: drinks containing 10 percent or more alcohol by volume are among the foods that need no 'best before' or 'use by' date at all, which covers Taiwanese rice wine at around 19.5 percent and most bottled cooking wines. Keep the bottle capped, cool, dark and away from the hob. An opened bottle goes flat and sherry-like over time as it oxidises, and a salted cooking wine holds up longer than a plain one.
en.fridge: Refrigeration is not needed and will not stop the oxidation that dulls an opened bottle — the cap and the dark do more than the cold does. A table wine you happen to be cooking with is a different case, because it is judged as a drink: an opened bottle of red or white is given only 1 to 3 days refrigerated. If you cook with real wine rather than with bottled cooking wine, work to that shorter clock.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for cooking wine and no reason to freeze it. Alcohol at this strength does not freeze solid in a domestic freezer, and the alcohol and, where present, the salt already preserve it. Use the freezer for things that actually need it.
spoilage: A flat, sherry-like or vinegary smell where there was a clean one
A colour that has darkened noticeably since the bottle was opened
Cloudiness or floating matter in a bottle that was clear
Mould around the neck or cap, usually in dried residue
tips: Cap it tightly — air, not time, is what flattens an opened bottle.
Keep it away from the hob; heat ages it fastest.
Decant into a smaller bottle when it is half empty to cut down on air.
If you are cooking with drinking wine, treat the open bottle as a drink, not a condiment.

faq.a: Not in a dangerous way. At 10 percent alcohol or more it is self-preserving; what fades is aroma. Keep it capped in a cool dark cupboard.

faq.q: Does cooking wine need to be refrigerated?
faq.a: No. Refrigeration is unnecessary and does not stop oxidation. A tight cap and a dark cupboard matter more.

faq.q: How long does an opened bottle of cooking wine last?
faq.a: There is no published figure. Judge it by smell and colour — it flattens gradually rather than spoiling. Salted versions hold up longer.

faq.q: Can you use leftover drinking wine for cooking?
faq.a: Yes, but it is on a much shorter clock: opened red or white wine is given only 1 to 3 days refrigerated, because it is judged as a drink.

zh.name: 料理米酒
zh.summary: 瓶裝料理用酒——台灣料理米酒、紹興酒、加鹽料理酒和葡萄基底的烹飪酒——沒有固定的保存期限。酒精濃度在 10% 以上時，它不是會危險腐敗的食品；蓋緊放在陰涼避光的櫥櫃就好。開封後失去的是香氣，不是安全。
zh.pantry: 櫥櫃就是對的位置，而誠實的答案是一條規則而不是數字：酒精濃度 10% 以上的飲品，屬於完全不需要標示有效日期的食品類別，而台灣料理米酒約 19.5%，多數瓶裝料理酒也在這個範圍內。請蓋緊、陰涼、避光、遠離爐火。開封後隨著氧化，酒會逐漸變扁、出現類似雪莉酒的味道，加鹽的料理酒又比一般的撐得久一些。
zh.fridge: 不需要冷藏，冷藏也擋不住讓開封酒變鈍的氧化——蓋子和避光比低溫更有用。但「拿來做菜的餐酒」是另一回事，因為它是以飲品的標準被評估的：開瓶後的紅白酒冷藏只給 1 到 3 天。如果你是用真正的葡萄酒下廚，請照那個比較短的時鐘走。
zh.freezer: 料理用酒沒有冷凍期限，也沒有冷凍的理由。這個濃度的酒精在家用冷凍庫不會凍硬，而酒精（以及加鹽款的鹽）本來就在保存它。冷凍庫留給真正需要的東西。
spoilage: 原本乾淨的酒香變成扁平的雪莉味或醋味
顏色比剛開瓶時明顯變深
原本清澈的瓶子變濁或出現漂浮物
瓶口或瓶蓋的乾漬處長霉
tips: 蓋緊——讓開封酒變扁的是空氣，不是時間。
遠離爐火，高溫讓它老化最快。
喝到剩一半時換小瓶裝，減少瓶內空氣。
如果是用餐酒下廚，就把那瓶當飲品而不是調味料看待。

faq.a: 不會以危險的方式壞掉。酒精 10% 以上能自我保存，流失的是香氣。蓋緊放陰涼避光的櫥櫃即可。
不用。冷藏沒有必要，也擋不住氧化。蓋緊和避光更重要。

faq.q: 開封的料理米酒可以放多久？
faq.a: 沒有已發表的數字。請用氣味和顏色判斷——它是逐漸變扁而不是腐敗。加鹽款撐得比較久。

faq.q: 喝剩的葡萄酒可以拿來做菜嗎？
faq.a: 可以，但時鐘短很多：開瓶後的紅白酒冷藏只給 1 到 3 天，因為它是以飲品的標準被評估的。
